fixture_cases.title: Ransomware encrypted departmental file shares after RDP compromise
fixture_cases.text: A domain admin account reused across systems was used to log in over RDP from an external address. The attacker deleted volume shadow copies with vssadmin, then a payload renamed more than 4,000 files on two file servers to a .locked extension and dropped a ransom note. Both servers were isolated, the account was disabled and passwords were reset, and data was restored from offline backups. Lesson learned: enforce MFA on remote access and restrict RDP exposure.

fixture_cases.title: Phishing invoice with macro-enabled document launching a PowerShell downloader
fixture_cases.text: An accounting user opened an emailed invoice in .docm format and enabled macros. The macro started powershell.exe with an encoded command that downloaded a loader from a compromised WordPress site. The sender domain was blocked, the attachment quarantined and the host reimaged. Lesson learned: block macros from the internet by policy and add the sender infrastructure to the mail filter.

fixture_cases.title: Credential dumping against LSASS on a domain controller
fixture_cases.text: EDR reported a process opening a handle to lsass.exe with read access on a domain controller. Investigation found rundll32 invoking comsvcs.dll MiniDump to write a memory dump to the temp folder. The dump was collected, affected privileged accounts were reset and the krbtgt password was rotated twice. Lesson learned: enable credential guard and alert on LSASS access by non-system processes.

fixture_cases.title: VPN gateway password guessing from rotating IP addresses
fixture_cases.text: The VPN concentrator logged thousands of failed authentications for several accounts from many source addresses within one hour, followed by a successful login for one user from the same ASN. The source ranges were blocked, the affected user's sessions were revoked and the password reset. Lesson learned: require MFA on the VPN and rate limit failed logons per account.

fixture_cases.title: HTTPS beaconing to a newly registered domain from a workstation
fixture_cases.text: Network telemetry showed a workstation connecting every 60 seconds with small random jitter to a domain registered three days earlier over TLS. The process was a signed binary loaded with an unsigned DLL. The domain was blocked at DNS, a memory image was captured and an EDR scan removed the implant. Lesson learned: monitor newly registered domains and inspect outbound TLS from servers and workstations.

fixture_cases.title: Large upload of company documents to a personal cloud storage account
fixture_cases.text: A user account transferred 40 GB to an external cloud storage service using the rclone utility outside working hours. Proxy logs showed sustained uploads to the provider's API endpoint. The account was disabled, the tool removed and the data owner informed. Lesson learned: restrict file synchronisation tools and alert on abnormal outbound volume.

fixture_cases.title: Persistence through a scheduled task created by a trojanized installer
fixture_cases.text: After a user ran a software installer downloaded from a file sharing site, a scheduled task named after a system component was created with schtasks to run a script stored under AppData at every logon. The task and script were removed and the installer hash was blocked. Lesson learned: audit new scheduled tasks and restrict script execution from user profile folders.

fixture_cases.title: Internal vulnerability scanner flagged as network port scan
fixture_cases.text: The IDS raised a high severity port scan alert from an internal address. The source was the approved vulnerability scanner running its weekly authenticated scan window. No malicious activity was found and the alert was closed as a false positive. Lesson learned: tag the scanner address and scheduled windows so scan activity is suppressed or downgraded.
